newsitem.title: USA: "Cats" breaks Broadway record for longevity.
newsitem.headline: "Cats" breaks Broadway record for longevity.

text.p: The musical "Cats" was poised to make history on Thursday as the longest-running show on Broadway.
Andrew Lloyd Webber's hit musical about a pack of felines learning to transcend their catty ways in a quest for moral purr-fection was set to present its record-breaking 6,138th performance.
It thus surpasses "A Chorus Line" as the longest-running production in the famed entertainment district.
"Cats" premiered in London in 1981, moving to New York a year later. More than 8.25 million people have seen the show, which won seven 1983 Tonys, including Best Musical.
Before the historic show Thursday, "Cats" creators offered their explanations for the production's longevity.
"The key is the poetry," said Lloyd Webber, adding that his mother used to read him "Old Possum's Book of Practical Cats" by T.S. Eliot, the inspiration for the musical.
"There's a mystery about cats worldwide. There's a love of domestic cats, and an interest in cats as ritual creatures and religious icons," said director Trevor Nunn.
"It's a universal story everyone can understand," said Susan Powers, a chorus member in the New York production for 15 years.
The show has used a tonne of yak hair for wigs, 5,782 knee pads to protect its 231 performers and more than 48,000 condoms to protect body microphones from perspiration.
The performance Thursday night was to be followed by an outdoor laser show and a gala party for casts and crews from all the shows now playing on Broadway, producers said.
